newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - May 20. [CORRECTED 13:10 GMT]
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - May 20. [CORRECTED 13:10 GMT]

text.p: The following stories were reported in Tuesday's electronic version of The Wall Street Journal:
* President Clinton is expected to win House approval of a balanced-budget plan on Tuesday, but it will not come with support from Democratic Leader Richard Gephardt.
* Delgratia Mining Corp said it has found "insignificant" amounts of gold at its Nevada property.
* General Motors Corp has reached an agreement that could pave the way for it to win a car-making project in China.
* Golfer Tiger Woods has signed a five-year deal to be a spokesman for American Express Co..
* Walt Disney Co's ABC released a revamped fall schedule of primetime shows.
* The Federal Trade Commission said internal Staples Inc documents show that its plan to buy Office Depot Inc is an effort to stem declining profit margins by removing an aggressive rival.
* The Dow Jones Industrials rose as investors focused on Tuesday's Federal Reserve meeting on interest rates.
* The Justice Department is seeking more information from Microsoft Corp on its planned acquisition of WebTV network.
* Microsoft co-founder Paul Allen plans to trade his 47.5 percent stake in Ticketmaster Group Inc for shares in HSN Inc (corrects from Home Shopping Network Inc).
* Mobil Corp and Amoco Corp saw their stock rise on reports they are discussing a possible merger of their U.S. refining and marketing units.
* McDonald's Corp plans to increase advertising to make their 55-cent sandwich promotion more clear to consumers.
* Esquire Editor in Chief Edward Kosner is leaving the magazine.
* Schering-Plough Corp has agreed to aquire the animal-health unit of Mallinckrodt Inc for $405 million.
* Electronic Data Systems Corp expects to post second quarter profits of between $0.43 and $0.45 per share, which falls short of analysts' expectations.
* Heard on the Street: In today's post-industrial, post-modern era, with more than 9,000 public companies jostling for attention in an exuberant bull market, corporate names have gone quirky.
* Credit Markets: Treasury-bond prices edged slightly lower in quiet trading, as investors and traders awaited another meeting of Federal Reserve policy makers today.
